ties.applies_to: persons "returned with an equal and the highest number of votes" at the state canvass, for offices other than the executive branch
ties.steps: the board of state canvassers (Governor, Secretary of State, Auditor, Treasurer, Attorney General) decides by lot which of the tied persons is elected; where a recount is held (section 32-1119) and still leaves a tie, section 32-1122(5) gives the same lot

sources.quote: If any two or more persons are returned with an equal and the highest number of votes, the board of state canvassers shall decide by lot which of such persons is elected except for officers elected to the executive branch.

If a recount after a general or special election results in any two or more persons having an equal and the highest number of votes for an office canvassed by the board of state canvassers, the board shall decide by lot which of such persons is elected, except officers elected to the executive department.

ties.note: The text does not name U.S. Senate, U.S. House, presidential electors or the Legislature. Section 32-1037 gives the board the canvass of "all officers and issues certified to the election commissioner or county clerk by the Secretary of State", and 32-1038(1) says the presidential-elector canvass counts the electors' votes, so these offices are read as "persons returned" to the board [inferred]. The lot is a drawing by the board; the statute does not say how.

ties.applies_to: Governor, Secretary of State, Auditor of Public Accounts, State Treasurer, Attorney General or other officer elected to an executive department, after a recount
ties.steps: a recount comes first (an automatic recount under 32-1119 unless waived); if the recount leaves two or more persons with an equal and the highest number of votes, the Legislature chooses one of them for the office; for Governor, the Lieutenant Governor is the candidate for Lieutenant Governor chosen by the person the Legislature selects

sources.quote: If a recount after a general or special election results in any two or more persons having an equal and the highest number of votes for the office of the Governor, Secretary of State, Auditor of Public Accounts, State Treasurer, Attorney General, or other officer elected to an executive department, the Legislature shall choose one of such persons for the office.

If any two or more persons are returned with an equal and the highest number of votes, the board of state canvassers shall decide by lot which of such persons is elected except for officers elected to the executive branch.

ties.note: Public Service Commission members are canvassed by the Legislature (32-1039) but are not named in 32-1122(4); whether a PSC tie goes to the Legislature or to the board's lot is not stated [unread as to that office]. Other statewide offices elected by district (Regents, State Board of Education) were not separately traced; they are read with the board-of-state-canvassers lot [inferred].

ties.applies_to: county, city, village or school district office at a general or special election, after a recount
ties.steps: a recount comes first (automatic under 32-1119 unless waived); if it leaves two or more persons with an equal and the highest number of votes, the county canvassing board determines by lot, in the presence of the candidates or their representatives, which is elected; the election commissioner or county clerk notifies the candidates by certified mail to appear

sources.quote: If a recount after a general or special election results in any two or more persons having an equal and the highest number of votes for the same county, city, village, or school district office, the county canvassing board shall, in the presence of the candidates or their representatives, determine by lot which of the candidates shall be elected.

ties.note: State general law only. Home-rule city charters (for example Omaha and Lincoln) and special districts other than school districts (natural resources districts, community college areas, and the like) were not read, and 32-1122 does not name them.

ties.applies_to: a party primary: county, city, village or school district nomination (county canvassing board) and nominations canvassed by the board of state canvassers, after a recount
ties.steps: a recount comes first; if it leaves two or more persons with an equal and the highest number of votes for the nomination, the county canvassing board (local nominations) or the board of state canvassers (nominations it canvasses) decides by lot which is nominated
ties.who: the county canvassing board, or the board of state canvassers

sources.quote: (3) If a recount after a primary election results in any two or more persons having an equal and the highest number of votes for nomination to an office canvassed by the board of state canvassers, the board shall decide by lot which of such persons is nominated.

If a recount after a primary election results in any two or more persons having an equal and the highest number of votes for the same nomination for the same county, city, village, or school district office, the county canvassing board shall, in the presence of the candidates or their representatives, determine by lot which of the candidates shall be nominated.

ties.note: Subsection (3) does not except executive-department nominations, so a primary tie for governor and other executive offices goes to the board's lot, not to the Legislature.

ties.applies_to: a ballot measure (initiative, referendum, constitutional amendment) that ties
ties.steps: no provision found for a tied vote on a measure
ties.note: Read: Chapter 32 sections 32-1031 (county canvass), 32-1037 and 32-1038 (state canvass, including the "declare those measures carried which have received the required percentage of votes" sentence), 32-1039, 32-1040, 32-1118 to 32-1122 (recounts and tie) and 32-1414 (measures counted and canvassed like candidates). None says what a tie on a measure does; a measure that does not get the required percentage is not carried. The chapter was not searched section by section outside the canvass and recount provisions, so an absence elsewhere is not excluded.

threshold.percent_of: the votes received by the candidate who received the highest number of votes (one seat), or who received the fewest votes qualifying for nomination or election (two or more seats)
threshold.conditions: applies where more than 500 votes were cast for the office; 500 or fewer votes cast: see the next rule (two percent)
threshold.in_words: a losing candidate is entitled to a recount where the margin is one percent or less of the votes received by the winning candidate (the last qualifying candidate where there are several seats), if more than 500 votes were cast for the office

recounts.cost_bearer: the political subdivisions involved in the recount
recounts.waiver: any losing candidate may waive the recount by filing a written statement with the Secretary of State, election commissioner or county clerk with whom he or she filed

sources.quote: (1) Any candidate who failed to be nominated or elected shall be entitled to a recount if it appears, as evidenced by the abstract of votes, that the candidate failed to be nominated or elected by one of the following margins: (a) If more than five hundred votes were cast for the office, one percent or less of the votes received by the candidate:
All expenses of a recount under this section shall be paid by those political subdivisions involved in the recount.

recounts.note: The section is headed "Automatic recount" and the recount is made by the county canvassing board without a request, subject to the candidate's waiver. Its words are "any candidate" and it does not list offices, so the kinds are read as every office on a primary or general ballot [inferred]; the margin is measured from the votes of the winning (or last qualifying) candidate, not from the total cast. Section 32-1119(4) says recounts for candidates who filed with the Secretary of State are made on the fifth Wednesday after the election; other recounts are made by the county canvassing board after its canvass (32-1119(5)).

threshold.percent_of: the votes received by the candidate who received the highest number of votes (one seat), or who received the fewest votes qualifying for nomination or election (two or more seats)
threshold.conditions: applies only where 500 or fewer votes were cast for the office
threshold.in_words: a losing candidate is entitled to a recount where the margin is two percent or less of the votes received by the winning candidate (the last qualifying candidate where there are several seats), if 500 or fewer votes were cast for the office

recounts.cost_bearer: the political subdivisions involved in the recount
recounts.waiver: any losing candidate may waive the recount by filing a written statement with the Secretary of State, election commissioner or county clerk with whom he or she filed

sources.quote: (b) If five hundred or fewer votes were cast for the office, two percent or less of the votes received by the candidate:

Any losing candidate may waive his or her right to a recount by filing a written statement with the Secretary of State, election commissioner, or county clerk with whom he or she made his or her filing.

threshold.conditions: available where the candidate lost by more than the margin in 32-1119
threshold.in_words: a losing candidate who lost by more than the automatic-recount margin may ask for a recount at his or her own expense, at one hundred dollars per precinct voting in the contest, refunded if the recount makes the candidate the winner

who_may_request: the losing candidate, by certified written request filed with the filing officer not later than the third day after the county canvassing board or the board of state canvassers concludes
recounts.cost_bearer: the requester ($100 per precinct voting in the contest, paid with the request; refunded if the recount determines the candidate to be the winner)

sources.quote: If any candidate failed to be nominated or elected by more than the margin provided in section 32-1119[...], the losing candidate may submit a certified written request for a recount at such candidate's expense.
The cost of the recount shall be one hundred dollars per precinct voting in the contest.
If the recount determines the candidate to be the winner, all costs which he or she paid shall be refunded.

recounts.note: No upper limit on the margin is stated in 32-1121. The deadline and the payment are conditions of the request.

threshold.conditions: none stated; the apparent loser files a petition by the fourth Monday after the election with a corporate surety bond of $2,500
threshold.in_words: the apparent loser at a general election for a seat in the Legislature may secure a recount by petitioning the Secretary of State, with a $2,500 bond to pay costs if the recount does not change the result

who_may_request: the apparent loser at a general election for a seat in the Legislature, by petition in duplicate filed with the Secretary of State
recounts.cost_bearer: the petitioner if he or she loses (costs are adjudged against the petitioner under 32-1116; $2,500 bond); if the petitioner wins, the state, county or other political subdivision

sources.quote: The apparent loser at a general election for a seat in the Legislature may secure a recount of the ballots cast at such election by filing a petition for a recount in duplicate with the Secretary of State no later than the fourth Monday after the election.

The petition shall be accompanied by a corporate surety bond in the penal sum of two thousand five hundred dollars conditioned for the payment of costs pursuant to section 32-1116 if the recount fails to change the results of the election.

recounts.note: This is a recount separate from the automatic recount of 32-1119, which also reaches Legislature seats.

threshold.in_words: no recount provision for presidential electors found by name; section 32-1119 speaks of "any candidate"

recounts.note: Sections 32-1119 and 32-1121 say "candidate" and do not name presidential electors, who are voted as a party's slate; whether they come within these sections was not settled by the text read [unread as to that point].

threshold.in_words: no recount provision for a ballot measure found

recounts.note: Read 32-1118 to 32-1122 (the sections the chapter index titles as recounts) and 32-1414 (measures canvassed like candidates). The recount sections speak only of candidates; the only contest for a measure listed is the court contest of 32-1108 (not read for recounts). An absence from these sections is not confirmed for the whole chapter.

unread.what: recall elections (32-1308: a tie leaves the official in office; a margin of one percent or less between removal and retention brings an ordered recount unless the official declines in writing)
unread.reason: read but not recorded as a rule: a recall is not one of the kinds on the closed list; it is noted here for the orchestrator

unread.what: election contest chapters (32-1101 to 32-1117), home-rule charters, and the primary-election chapter beyond the recount articles
unread.reason: outside the brief (contest chapters) or not read

notes: Nebraska settles a tie only after a recount: 32-1122 begins "If a recount ... results in" a tie. 32-1038(2) gives the board of state canvassers a lot with no recount condition, so both are cited. Executive-department offices (governor, secretary of state, auditor, treasurer, attorney general) go to the Legislature, not to a lot.
Nebraska's automatic recount margin is measured against the winning candidate's votes, not the total votes cast, and is one percent (two percent where 500 or fewer votes were cast).
